newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sumitomo 1st half copper sales fall.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo 1st half copper sales fall.

text.p: Sumitomo Corp said on Tuesday that its copper sales from April to September, the first half of the 1996/97 business year, fell to 181.2 billion yen, down by 243.3 billion yen from the same period a year earlier.

The 57 percent slide in copper sales came in the wake of a major copper scandal at the trade house, which fired its chief copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka in June and accused him of racking up a $2.6 billion loss from unauthorised trades.
The scandal also precipitated a tumble in world copper prices in May and June of more than one-third to their lowest levels in 2 1/2 years.
A Sumitomo official told reporters at a news conference that the trade house expected copper sales in the full 1996/97 financial year to be less than 300 billion yen.

Sumitomo recorded a net loss in the April-September half of 212.12 billion yen on a consolidated basis, reflecting the impact of its copper trading losses. The trade house expected a consolidated net loss of 147 billion yen for the full fiscal year.
